Article Title: A vitamin clue to stroke in the young? Bengaluru study finds low B6 levels
Article Text:
Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.

NEW DELHI: A vitamin that helps the body process proteins and regulate important chemical reactions may offer a new clue to why young adults suffer strokes. A study by researchers in Bengaluru has found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke than in healthy people of a similar age.Ahead of World Stroke Day on October 29, the findings draw attention to a possible factor associated with stroke in young adults. The study compared 171 young adults who had suffered an ischaemic stroke, caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain, with 249 healthy controls.Median vitamin B6 levels in stroke patients were 40.9 nmol/L, compared with 65.6 nmol/L in the control group. Vitamin B6 insufficiency, defined by the researchers as levels below 30 nmol/L, was found in 12.3% of stroke patients, compared with just 0.7% of healthy controls.Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach.Prof Manjari Tripathi, head of the department of neurology at AIIMS, said vitamin B6 is essential for homocysteine metabolism. “Low vitamin B6 levels can impair this process, allowing homocysteine to rise. Elevated homocysteine can damage blood vessels, promote inflammation and contribute to clot formation, increasing stroke risk.Maintaining adequate vitamin B6 levels through a balanced diet is important,” she said.The Bengaluru study adds to evidence linking vitamin B6 levels with stroke risk, but whether improving these levels can prevent strokes remains unclear. Dr Pravin Gupta, chairman, Marengo Asia international institute of neuro and spine, said the study was significant because vitamin B6 levels can be measured through a blood test. “However, this study shows an association, not proof that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke. Further research is needed,” he said.The researchers, led by scientists from the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, found that lower vitamin B6 levels were independently associated with higher odds of ischaemic stroke even after accounting for other factors. Among stroke patients, vitamin B6 levels were strongly inversely correlated with homocysteine, an amino acid associated with blood vessel health.Published inin 2026, the case-control study adds to research into factors associated with stroke among younger adults. However, it cannot establish whether low vitamin B6 contributes to stroke, results from other health or dietary factors, or reflects an underlying process. Further studies are needed to validate the findings.The results do not establish that vitamin B6 supplements can prevent stroke or that routine testing for the vitamin should be recommended for young adults.
Article Summary: Vitamin B6 is found in liver, fish such as tuna and salmon, chicken, chickpeas, sunflower seeds, pistachios, potatoes, bananas and spinach. Researchers in Bengaluru found significantly lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults who had an ischaemic stroke.

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Congress on Thursday took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the legislative council elections. The final result, which came after more than 40 hours of counting, forced Fadnavis to delete a tweet he had posted the previous day, mocking the Congress for failing to win any seat in the MLC polls.On Wednesday, PM Modi had posted a tweet mocking the Congress for failing to open its account despite the elections being held using ballot papers.The Congress had reacted sharply and dared to hold all elections using ballot papers, asking how many seats the party had won.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale in the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency by 3,271 votes, securing 67,231 votes against his rival's 63,960.Also read - 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results Fadnavis had posted the tweet in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dig at the Congress on X.“By deleting the tweet, Fadnavis has once again preserved Savarkar's legacy! Even before the full results were in hand, in a show of firing a big arrow, Fadnavis tweeted.But that very arrow turned back and pierced straight into his chest! In the end, he was forced to delete the tweet,” the Maharashtra Congress said on X.“Mr. Fadnavis, scared already at this stage? This is just the trailer! In 2029, the people of Maharashtra will drop such a political bombshell on you that even this tweet of today will come back to haunt you! All the best, Mr. Fadnavis! Get ready for the next jolt,” it added.Wanjari, the sitting MLC, secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960. The result dealt a setback to the BJP in Nagpur, the hometown of Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, both of whom had campaigned extensively for Kohale.The Congress also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states. Modi had questioned the Congress's tally, pointing out that the polls were conducted using ballot papers."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" Modi wrote in a post on X.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera responded by challenging the prime minister to commit to using ballot papers in future Lok Sabha and assembly elections."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJP’s electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," Khera wrote on X.He also demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the restoration of what he alleged were 13.3 crore illegally deleted voters, and action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also criticised Fadnavis over the deleted post, pointing to the BJP's defeat in Nagpur, where the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) headquarters is located."Respected Devendra Fadnavis Saheb, In the Nagpur Graduates Constituency, where you yourself took personal interest and went door-to-door to persuade the rebels to withdraw, in that very Nagpur constituency, in the area where the RSS headquarters is located, the BJP had to face defeat—the meaning of this is clear…… It is indeed regrettable that you had to delete your tweet; but the immense ego of power evident in your deleted tweet is not good at all. Anyway, I can understand. Perhaps you forgot that the election was held via ballot, so the tweet might have been made prematurely… Congratulations to the victorious candidate Abhijit Wanjarri, thanks to the graduates who gave their blessings in the form of votes, and best wishes to all the contesting candidates as well!" Pawar wrote on X.With Wanjari's victory, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) won three of the five Maharashtra Legislative Council seats contested on October 23, while the BJP-led Mahayuti secured two.NCP (SP) candidates Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav and Pratapsinh Patil won the Pune Graduates’ and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Graduates’ constituencies, respectively. Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade secured the Pune Teachers’ seat.The Nagpur result followed more than 40 hours of counting. Kohale had led Wanjari after the second round, but neither candidate secured the required quota through first-preference votes. Wanjari eventually overtook his rival during the subsequent elimination rounds as preferential votes were transferred.The outcome dealt a setback to the BJP in a constituency it had traditionally held. Gadkari represented the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council for 24 years, from 1990 to 2014.The results have triggered a political exchange between the BJP and opposition parties over electoral performance and the use of electronic voting machines. While Modi cited the ballot-paper polls to question the Congress's performance, the party has used the results to renew its demand for ballot papers in future elections.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Congress took a swipe at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis after the party retained the Nagpur Graduates’ constituency in the legislative council elections. The final result came after more than 40 hours of counting. The Congress also targeted PM Narendra Modi over his remarks on the party's performance in the Legislative Council elections held across four states.

Are banks closed on Karwa Chauth

Can you use banking services on a bank holiday?

NEW DELHI: Planning a quick trip to the bank today? You might want to check the holiday calendar first.The festive season brings a fresh round of bank holidays, but closures are not the same across India, as they depend on the festivals and regional occasions observed in each state.Today, October 29, banks in Himachal Pradesh are closed for Karwa Chauth. But if you are elsewhere in the country, the holiday schedule may be different. Therefore, a quick check before stepping out for your bank related errands could save you an unnecessary trip to the branch.After the Karwa Chauth holiday in Himachal Pradesh on October 29, Gujarat is set to see bank closures on October 31 to mark Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.Bank customers will also need to keep track of the holidays scheduled for November, when several festivals and regional observances are expected to affect branch operations in different states. The list includes Diwali and related celebrations, Ningol Chakkouba, Wangala Festival, Chhath Puja, Igas-Bagwal, Seng Kut Snem, Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kanakadasa Jayanthi.The dates and closures will vary depending on the state and the festival being observed.Bank customers need to check the schedule for their location, as closures depend on the regional festival or occasion being observed.Apart from festival-related closures, scheduled and non-scheduled banks also observe holidays on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month, in line with the Reserve Bank of India's holiday schedule.A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services. ATMs, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), internet banking and mobile banking applications remain available for routine transactions, including fund transfers, bill payments and account management.The main inconvenience is for transactions that require a visit to a physical branch. Customers planning large cash deposits, cheque processing, demand drafts or other branch-dependent work may have to wait until their branch reopens.With several holidays scheduled across October and November, checking the applicable state calendar before visiting a branch can help customers plan their banking requirements and avoid delays.
Article Summary: The festive season brings a fresh round of bank holidays, but closures are not the same across India. Closures depend on the festivals and regional occasions observed in each state. The dates and closures will vary depending on the state and the festival being observed. A branch closure does not mean customers lose access to all banking services.

Article Title: MLC election results: NDA wins 16, Congress gets 1, SP bags 5; state-wise results and key wins
Article Text:
The biennial elections for these Graduate and Teacher constituencies across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, and Maharashtra were held via ballot papers on October 23, 2026, with counting beginning on October 27, 2026.

Here is a state-wise look at the latest results and counting trends.

Karnataka (4 seats): BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four, Congress draws blank

Uttar Pradesh (11 seats): BJP wins four seats, SP secures two

Bihar (8 seats): Jan Suraaj opens account, RJD defeats BJP veteran

Maharashtra (5 seats): Congress retains Nagpur graduates’ seat, defeats BJP

NEW DELHI: Congress faced a major setback in the legislative council elections on Wednesday, failing to secure a victory in the seats declared so far across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra, even as counting continued in several constituencies.The biggest setback for the Congress came in Karnataka, where it failed to win a single seat despite being in power in the state. The BJP -JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats, with the BJP retaining three constituencies and the JD(S) wresting the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress. The defeat was particularly significant for the ruling party as it lost its sitting seat in Bengaluru Teachers’ and failed to make gains in any of the three BJP-held constituencies.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins, while in Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its legislative council account by defeating the Congress. The RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP.Counting for 28 legislative council seats across Uttar Pradesh (11), Bihar (8), Maharashtra (5) and Karnataka (4) began on Tuesday following polling on October 23.The elections were held for graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, with results declared for several seats and counting continuing in others.The BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats in Karnataka, dealing a setback to the ruling Congress. The BJP retained the North-East Teachers’, South-East Graduates’ and West Graduates’ constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachers’ seat from the Congress.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes in Bengaluru Teachers’. Ranganath secured 10,810 votes against Puttanna’s 9,902.BJP’s Shashil G Namoshi retained North-East Teachers’ by 3,297 votes, securing his fifth victory from the constituency with 15,596 votes against Congress candidate Sharanappa Mattur’s 12,299.In South-East Graduates’, BJP candidate K M Suresh defeated Congress nominee Shashi Hulikunte Mutt by 23,098 votes. Sitting BJP MLC S V Sankanur retained West Graduates’, defeating Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai by 9,323 votes.The results marked a clean sweep for the opposition alliance, with the Congress failing to win a single seat despite campaigning by chief minister D K Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and other senior leaders.However, the results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government or significantly alter the balance of power in the 75-member Legislative Council.The BJP won six of the 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, while the Samajwadi Party secured five. The BJP won the Agra Graduates’, Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’, Lucknow Teachers’, Meerut Teachers’, Meerut Graduates’ and Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituencies.The Samajwadi Party won the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’, Varanasi Teachers’ and Agra-Aligarh Teachers’ constituencies.In the Agra Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate Manvendra Pratap Singh (Guruji) was declared elected.The BJP retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers’ seat, with its candidate Hari Singh Dhillon defeating SP nominee Danish Akhtar by 17,676 votes. Dhillon secured 21,672 votes against Akhtar’s 3,996 after all five rounds of counting.The BJP also won the Lucknow Teachers’ constituency, where its candidate Umesh Dwivedi defeated SP’s Sushil Kumar by 6,992 votes. Dwivedi secured 13,179 votes against Kumar’s 8,371.In Meerut, the BJP won both the Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies. Its candidates Dinesh Kumar Goyal and Shri Chand Sharma were declared winners in the Graduates’ and Teachers’ seats, respectively.The BJP also retained the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, with its candidate Dhruv Tripathi defeating Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes. Tripathi secured 14,887 votes against Yadav’s 14,580.However, Yadav alleged that the election had been manipulated to ensure his defeat. Claiming that around 1,000 votes had been stolen, he said he would approach the Election Commission and the court to challenge the result. He also demanded a forensic examination of 1,612 votes counted in the fourth round, alleging irregularities in the counting process.The MLC polls are being viewed as a prestige battle between the ruling BJP and the opposition SP ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Voting for the 11 seats, comprising five Graduates’ and six Teachers’ constituencies, was held on Friday, with counting beginning at 8 am on Tuesday.The Bihar Legislative Council elections delivered several upsets, with five sitting MLCs losing their seats and the Jan Suraaj Party securing its maiden victory in the Upper House.Of the eight seats, which went to polls on October 23, the BJP won three, Independents secured two, while the RJD, Jan Suraaj Party and NDA partner JD(U) won one seat each.Jan Suraaj Party candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha in the Darbhanga Teachers’ constituency, marking the party’s first win in the Bihar Legislative Council.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut Teachers’ seat, defeating CPI MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh, who had the support of the INDIA bloc.In another major upset, RJD candidate Sanjeev Kumar defeated veteran BJP MLC Nawal Kishore Yadav in the Patna Teachers’ constituency, ending the latter’s long hold on the seat.Independent candidate Rahul Raj also defeated sitting MLC Afaq Ahmed in the Saran Teachers’ constituency.Meanwhile, JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar retained the Patna Graduates’ seat for a fourth consecutive term, defeating his rivals despite a challenge from within his party. BJP candidates Sarvesh Kumar and N K Yadav retained the Darbhanga Graduates’ and Kosi Graduates’ seats, respectively.Independent candidate Bansi Dhar Brajwasi also retained the Tirhut Graduates’ constituency, while two other seats went to the BJP and Independents as part of the overall tally.The Congress, which contested five seats, failed to win any and is now left with just one member in the 75-member Bihar Legislative Council.The polls saw 90 candidates contesting four Graduates’ constituencies and 60 candidates in four Teachers’ constituencies. The four Graduates’ seats had 4.92 lakh eligible voters, while the four Teachers’ constituencies had 40,253 voters.The BJP-led ruling Mahayuti won two seats in Maharashtra, while the opposition NCP (SP) bagged two, as results were declared for all five Legislative Council seats.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates’ constituency, ending more than 40 hours of counting. Wanjari secured 67,231 votes against Kohale’s 63,960.Also read: Congress opens account in MLC polls as Abhijit Wanjari retains Nagpur seat after nail-biting contest Kohale, a former MLA, had led Wanjari by 4,294 votes after the second round of counting on Wednesday. However, with no candidate securing the required quota through first-preference votes, the counting proceeded to second-preference votes, allowing Wanjari to overtake his rival during the elimination rounds.Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade emerged victorious in the Pune Teachers’ constituency.In the Pune Graduates’ constituency, NCP (SP) candidate Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav won, while party candidate Pratapsinh Patil secured victory in the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Graduates’ constituency.The polls, held on October 23, saw 182 candidates contesting across three Graduates’ and two Teachers’ constituencies. The results were closely watched amid rebel candidates, alliance differences and efforts by the BJP-led Mahayuti and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi to consolidate support.
Article Summary: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four legislative council seats in Karnataka. RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachers’ seat from the BJP. In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins.

NEW DELHI: Striking a discordant note among a clutch of petitions challenging the Transgender Amendment Act for denying right to gender self-determination, an all-women NGO Wednesday appealed to the Supreme Court not to confer trans-women, biological males identifying as females, the spectrum of constitutional rights guaranteed to biological women.‘Women’s Declaration International India’ through senior advocate Amit Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that “self-professed or socio-cultural gender identity or certificate or document cannot change a person’s biological sex or enable a biological male to access the entire spectrum of rights, protections and entitlements created specifically for biological females. ” Differentiating between sex and gender, the petitioner said, “Sex and gender identity are distinct; gender identity concerns a person’s deeply felt internal experience, while sex is the stable immutable biological category on which numerous constitutional and statutory protections for women are premised.”SC asked Centre to respond to the petition with a comprehensive affidavit that also dealt with the other petitions challenging the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026.SG Tushar Mehta said a comprehensive affidavit is being drafted but gave an indication of what would be govt’s stand in defence of the erasure of gender self-determination clause, which was replaced by medically determined gender.He asked: “Can a transwoman be permitted to compete in a sporting event for women? Should a policewoman conduct physical search of a person with male genitals but perceives himself to be a woman? If a biologically male criminal perceives himself to be a woman, should police be barred from arresting him after sunset?”Drawing the court’s attention to a recent incident in the US relating to a transgender inmate, who perceives himself to be a woman but impregnated two women inmates, Mehta said several aspects needed to be kept in mind while adjudicating the petitions.A male becoming a trans-woman will violate affirmative measures for women under the Constitution, equal opportunity to women in employment, women’s bodily privacy and personal security in sex-segregated spaces and criminal law safeguards, the petitioner said.
Article Summary: An all-women NGO has appealed to the Supreme Court not to confer trans-women, biological males identifying as females, the spectrum of constitutional rights guaranteed to biological women. ‘Women’s Declaration International India’ through senior advocate Amit Sibal told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that ‘self-professed or socio-cultural gender identity or certificate or document cannot change a person’’

Article Title: Junk food’s impact may go beyond the weighing scale
Article Text:
Junk food impact on health

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A packet of chips after school, a cookie between meals or a burger as a treat may seem harmless. But a new study suggests that eating more ultra-processed foods may be linked to changes in how children’s brains respond to food, as well as greater gains in body fat over the following year.Published in JAMA Network Open this month, the study followed 46 children who were at a healthy weight at the start. Researchers found that children who got a larger share of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods (UPFs) showed stronger responses in a brain region linked to reward, motivation and habit formation when they saw pictures of tempting foods such as cookies and French fries.These stronger brain responses were linked to greater increases in body mass index (BMI) and body fat over the next year. Children who ate more UPFs also showed an increase in waist size.The findings raise a new concern in the debate over childhood obesity: could the way children’s brains respond to food be part of the link between eating highly processed foods and gaining weight?Dr Arun Gupta, convenor of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi) and co-author of the 2025 Lancet series on ultra-processed foods, said the findings should prompt a closer look at the foods children eat and how these products are marketed to them.He said repeated exposure to highly appealing foods could encourage habitual eating.The study, however, did not prove that children become addicted to food or that junk food directly changes their brains.The researchers also found that sugar alone may not explain the link. Many ultra-processed foods combine fat and carbohydrates, which can trigger a strong reward response in the brain. However, when researchers accounted for added-sugar intake, the link between UPF consumption and brain response weakened, suggesting that several factors may be involved.The findings come amid calls for tighter restrictions on advertising foods high in fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) to children. NAPi has sought amendments to the Press Council of India’s Norms of Journalistic Conduct 2022 to prohibit such advertising. The Press Council referred the proposal to the Union health ministry in May 2024, sought comments in June 2025 and sent a reminder in 2026, but NAPi says it is still awaiting a response.It has also written to the information and broadcasting ministry.Although the study was conducted in the US and its findings cannot be directly extrapolated to Indian children, it raises a key question: should tackling childhood obesity also mean addressing the advertising and food environments that shape children’s choices?
Article Summary: Eating more ultra-processed foods may be linked to changes in how children’s brains respond to food. Study followed 46 children who were at a healthy weight at the start of the study. Children who ate more UPFs also showed an increase in waist size. Findings raise a new concern in the debate over childhood obesity.

Article Title: Yet to test legality of logical discrepancy in SIR: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC said that while it upheld SIR in Bihar, it did not examine the legality of the ‘logical discrepancy’ criterion

SC: Can EC go beyond 2003 list to scrutinise logical discrepancy?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said that even though the validity of SIR in Bihar was upheld, the court had no occasion to test the legality of the ‘logical discrepancy’ criterion as it was not used during the Bihar exercise.When EC’s counsel referred to smooth conduct of Bihar and West Bengal elections after SIR, the bench said, “Logical discrepancy (mode for deletion) was first resorted to in West Bengal. We are yet to examine its validity. We will go into logical discrepancy in detail later.”When petitioner Anjali Bhardwaj’s counsel claimed that lakhs of voters were deleted from the draft Delhi rolls on grounds of ‘logical discrepancy’, the bench asked how EC could reopen entries in the 2003 voter list and issue notices for logical discrepancy.“In a voter enumeration exercise like SIR, EC has taken the 2003 voter list as the base. If that is so, how could it classify those whose names figured in that list as ineligible on grounds of logical discrepancy? Can EC go beyond the list and reopen it?” the bench asked.During the last hearing, the bench had suggested that EC examine putting additional filters to avoid mechanical issuance of notices under ‘logical discrepancy’.In a voter enumeration exercise like SIR, EC has taken the 2003 voter list as the base. If that is so, how could it classify those whose names figured in that list as ineligible on grounds of logical discrepancy? Can EC go beyond the list and reopen it?” the bench asked.During the last hearing, the bench had suggested that EC examine putting additional filters to avoid mechanical issuance of notices under ‘logical discrepancy’.Opposition INDIA bloc functionaries, led by Rahul Gandhi, have filed a joint petition challenging many issues, including the SIR process, and questioned the allegedly arbitrary non-inclusion of names because of ‘logical discrepancy’.In its May 27 judgment, SC had examined the following questions — whether EC had the power to conduct SIR; whether SIR had a legitimate purpose and the process was proportionate to the object to be achieved; and whether the SIR procedure was contrary to Representation of the People Act, 1951, and Registration of Electors Act, 1960 — and found that there was nothing amiss in the conduct of SIR or the process adopted to achieve the object of weeding out voters who had died, shifted house or had duplicate entries.SC had categorically ruled that the SIR exercise “neither stands in direct conflict with RP Act and 1960 Rules, nor does it detract from the constitutional imperative of free and fair elections”. It had said, “The impugned SIR exercise, as conducted, satisfies the requirements of proportionality. The measures adopted bear a rational nexus to the objective sought to be achieved, are not manifestly excessive, and are accompanied by sufficient procedural safeguards to prevent arbitrary exclusion.“We are equally satisfied that, in its object and design, the impugned SIR bears a direct nexus to the constitutional goal of free and fair elections. Free and fair elections do not rest merely upon the mechanics of polling. They equally depend upon the integrity, accuracy and purity of the electoral roll which forms the foundation of the democratic process.”
Article Summary: SC said that while it upheld SIR in Bihar, it did not examine the legality of the ‘logical discrepancy’ criterion. ‘Logical discrepancy (mode for deletion) was first resorted to in West Bengal. We are yet to examine its validity,’ the bench said.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: ‘He still has a lot to prove’: Waqar Younis makes bold claim on Jasprit Bumrah
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah (ANI Photo)

Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis has hailed Jasprit Bumrah as the standout bowler in modern-day white-ball cricket but believes the Indian fast bowler still has more to establish in the Test format.Despite Bumrah 's impressive record of 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7 and a strike rate of 42.8, Waqar feels the pacer has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers.“There’s no modern-day bowler of the same calibre as Bumrah with the white ball. Leave out Test cricket. He still has a lot to prove in Tests; he hasn’t played as much. There are plenty of others, like Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. You can’t ignore some of the English bowlers either. But when you talk about T20 and one-day cricket, I feel that in terms of impact, Bumrah always delivers in crunch scenarios. And that’s what matters,” Waqar said on the Shubhankar Mishra podcast.Waqar's assessment comes despite Bumrah's significant achievements in the longest format. The India pacer became the fastest Indian fast bowler to reach 50 Test wickets in 2018, accomplishing the milestone in his 11th match. He went on to claim his 100th Test wicket in his 24th appearance.Bumrah also became only the third Indian bowler to take a Test hat-trick in 2019. His performances in 2024 earned him the ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year award, while he finished the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy with 32 wickets in five Tests, a record haul for the series.The right-arm pacer has also been highly effective in England, taking 51 wickets in 11 Tests.One possible reason behind Waqar's assessment is Bumrah's limited availability in Test cricket compared with Australian quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. Injuries and workload management have affected his participation, and he is yet to play a Test for India this year.Bumrah is expected to return for India's two-match Test series in New Zealand next month, with a place in the World Test Championship final at stake.While questioning Bumrah's standing in Tests, Waqar was unequivocal about the Indian pacer's influence in ODIs and T20Is. He particularly remembered Bumrah's decisive contribution in India's six-run victory over Pakistan at the 2024 T20 World Cup in New York.Pakistan appeared firmly in control at 80/3 after 14 overs, needing only 40 runs from the final six overs to chase India's target of 120. Bumrah dismissed Mohammad Rizwan, triggering a collapse that helped India defend the modest total.Waqar believes that spell demonstrated why Bumrah is such a valuable asset in high-pressure situations, particularly when a captain needs a breakthrough.“Whenever an India captain is in trouble, he always gives the ball to Bumrah. Pakistan had no business losing in New York. The required rate was well under control. That over in which Bumrah dismissed Rizwan proved to be the difference. Impact players are the key players. A top player can motivate others who too feel that we have to match him,” said Waqar, who took 373 wickets in Test cricket for Pakistan.For Waqar, Bumrah's greatest strength in white-ball cricket is his ability to deliver when the stakes are highest, making him a decisive figure in crucial moments.
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah has taken 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.7. Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis believes the Indian fast bowler has not played enough red-ball cricket to be placed ahead of other leading fast bowlers. Bumra's greatest strength is his ability to deliver when the stakes are highest.

Article Title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ business ventures timeline: From Kansas City sports team investments in 2020 to Formula 1, restaurants and fitness brands
Article Text:
Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ business ventures timeline: From Kansas City sports team investments in 2020 to Formula 1, restaurants and fitness brands

How did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes start their business journey?

Which sports teams do Patrick and Brittany Mahomes own stakes in?

Patrick Mahomes is one of the biggest names in American football, but his business interests go far beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs. Alongside his wife, Brittany Mahomes, he has invested in professional sports teams, restaurants, fitness technology, and other businesses. Their journey began with investments in Kansas City sports and later expanded to international motorsports and consumer brands. While Patrick has used his NFL success to build his investment portfolio, Brittany has played an important role in women’s soccer as a founding owner of the Kansas City Current.One of the couple’s earliest major business moves came in 2020, when Patrick joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Royals, a Major League Baseball team. His stake has been widely reported at around 1%, although the exact ownership details have not been fully disclosed publicly. The investment gave the NFL star a place in professional baseball ownership while he continued to build his career with the Chiefs.In 2021, Patrick expanded his sports investments by joining the ownership group of Sporting Kansas City, a Major League Soccer club. The move strengthened his connection with the city where he plays football and added another professional team to his portfolio.Brittany was building her own business interests around the same time. She became a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current, a National Women’s Soccer League team established in 2020. Her involvement made women’s soccer an important part of the couple’s business story, while Patrick later joined the ownership group.Their investments were not limited to sports. Patrick also entered the restaurant business through KMO Burgers, a franchise partnership connected to Whataburger. The arrangement helped bring the Texas-based burger chain to the Kansas City area, giving the football star a business interest in the fast-food industry.These early ventures established a pattern that continued in later years. Rather than depending only on football contracts and endorsement deals, Patrick and Brittany began investing in businesses that could operate and grow beyond his playing career.Sports ownership has become one of the most visible parts of Patrick’s business portfolio. His investments include the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City, and the Kansas City Current, giving him connections to professional baseball and both men’s and women’s soccer.Patrick’s involvement with the Royals began in 2020, while he joined Sporting Kansas City’s ownership group in 2021. His investment in the Current followed in 2022, when he joined the club’s ownership group alongside Brittany and other investors. The Current announced his co-ownership in January 2023, describing him as the first active NFL player to hold an ownership stake in an NWSL club.The Current has also grown in reported financial value. Forbes valued the club at $75 million in 2024, $275 million in 2025, and $325 million in 2026. These figures show the rise in the team’s estimated value, although they do not reveal how much Patrick or Brittany personally made from their investments.Patrick also moved into international motorsports in October 2023, when he joined an investor group that acquired a 24% stake in the Alpine Formula 1 team. The group reportedly paid around $210 million for the combined stake, with other investors including NFL teammate Travis Kelce, actor Ryan Reynolds, golfer Rory McIlroy, and boxer Anthony Joshua.However, the $210 million investment was made by the group as a whole. Patrick’s individual contribution and ownership percentage have not been publicly disclosed, so it would be inaccurate to attribute the entire investment to him.Beyond sports teams, Patrick has developed interests in restaurants, fitness technology, and consumer products. His Whataburger franchise partnership is one example of his move into businesses that serve customers outside the sports world.Through KMO Burgers, Patrick became a franchise partner helping expand Whataburger in the Kansas City area. The investment gave him a connection to a well-known fast-food brand and added a local business venture to his portfolio.Patrick has also been linked to Throne Sport Coffee, a performance-focused coffee brand. Reports have described him as a lead investor and a major shareholder, although the precise size of his stake has not been publicly confirmed.Another notable investment is WHOOP, the wearable fitness technology company that makes devices used to track activity, recovery, and sleep. Patrick has been reported as an early investor in the company. WHOOP reached a reported valuation of $3.6 billion during a 2021 funding round, but that figure reflects the company’s valuation at that time, not the current value of Patrick’s investment.These ventures share a common theme. They connect Patrick’s public image as a professional athlete with products related to food, fitness, and performance. However, the amount he invested in each business and the returns he has received remain largely private.The couple’s business timeline shows how their interests have grown across different industries.In 2020, Patrick joined the Kansas City Royals’ ownership group, while Brittany became a founding co-owner of the Kansas City Current. These investments established their presence in professional sports ownership.In 2021, Patrick added Sporting Kansas City to his portfolio and expanded into the restaurant industry through his Whataburger franchise partnership. Around this period, he was also linked to investments in fitness technology, including WHOOP.In 2022, Patrick joined the Kansas City Current’s ownership group, building on Brittany’s existing role with the club. The team’s January 2023 announcement formally confirmed his co-ownership and highlighted the significance of an active NFL player investing in women’s professional soccer.Later in 2023, Patrick joined the investor group that acquired a minority stake in Alpine’s Formula 1 team. The move expanded his interests beyond Kansas City and into an international sport with a global audience.Their portfolio also extends beyond investments in operating businesses. Patrick founded 2PM Productions, a media production company, and established the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which supports initiatives benefiting children. These projects add media and philanthropy to his activities outside football.Brittany’s work with the Kansas City Current remains a key part of the couple’s business story. Her position as a founding owner gives her a direct role in women’s professional soccer, while Patrick’s investments span baseball, soccer, Formula 1, restaurants, and fitness technology.The couple’s individual ownership percentages and financial returns are not publicly available for most of these ventures. Still, their business history shows a clear move beyond football income and endorsements toward ownership interests across several industries. As Patrick continues his NFL career, these investments provide a foundation for business activities that can extend well beyond his time on the field.
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, have invested in sports teams, restaurants, fitness technology, and other businesses. Their first investments were in Kansas City sports and later expanded to international motorsports and consumer brands. While Patrick has used his NFL success to build his investment portfolio, Brittany has played an important role in women's soccer as a founding owner of the Kansas City Current.

Article Title: “Not all girls, especially girls from underserved communities”: How Naomi Osaka’s initiative is helping girls with disabilities build confidence and become future sports leaders
Article Text:
Naomi Osaka’s initiative is helping girls with disabilities build confidence and become future sports leaders

How Naomi Osaka’s Play Academy is expanding sports opportunities for girls with disabilities

How Naomi Osaka’s initiative is helping young women become leaders

Naomi Osaka wants more girls to experience the opportunities that sport gives her. Through Play Academy with Naomi Osaka, the four-time Grand Slam champion supports community organisations that help girls participate in sports and develop skills beyond the court. One example is NPO J Camp in Japan, where her initiative supports a project that gives girls with disabilities opportunities to play wheelchair basketball and explore leadership roles.The project, called Push for Future, began in 2024 with support from Play Academy. It gives Osaka’s wider mission a practical focus: helping girls build confidence through sport while creating opportunities for young women to guide the next generation.Osaka launched Play Academy in 2020 with Nike and Laureus Sport for Good. She drew on her own experience as a young tennis player and recognised that many girls do not have the same access to sport or role models.“I’ve been playing tennis since I was 3 years old, and it has changed my life. But I know not all girls, especially girls from underserved communities. have the same opportunities or role models that I’ve had, and I want to do something about it,” Osaka said in her statement on the official Play Academy website.Her initiative supports grassroots organisations rather than running every programme itself. In Japan, that support reaches J Camp, which uses wheelchair basketball to help girls with and without disabilities take part in sport.A report published by Play Academy on October 11, 2025, described how J Camp adapts its sessions with soft balls, hoops at different heights and a tambourine beneath a basket. These changes allow participants to try shots at their own pace. They can also choose their equipment and suggest changes to the rules.Makiko Harada, J Camp’s programme manager, explained the reason behind this approach in the October 11 report.“Children with disabilities often spend their days being helped, or holding back,” Harada said. “Here, they choose, decide and try on their own. Those small steps build self-confidence and self-efficacy.”The sessions give girls opportunities to make decisions for themselves instead of simply following instructions. They can try harder shots, create rules and encourage other participants. This is the kind of experience Play Academy aims to support by helping local organisations make sport more accessible.Play Academy’s support for J Camp also extends beyond participation. Through Push for Future, J Camp trains young women, including those with disabilities, in areas such as safeguarding and working with children with disabilities. They then become programme leaders and help run sessions.One of them, Yume, first discovered wheelchair basketball through a J Camp staff member when she was in high school. She joined the leadership programme in 2024 because she wanted to help create more places where everyone could enjoy sport, regardless of disability.In the Play Academy report, Yume described how the role helped her become more comfortable speaking with children and their parents.“I was so nervous speaking in front of the kids at first. But little by little, I started to go up and talk to them and their parents, and I’ve become more proactive. I’ve gained confidence—even if it’s just a little,” she said.Her experience shows how the programme can help young women develop skills they can use beyond the court. Harada also noted that seeing women take leadership roles can encourage girls to imagine themselves doing the same.According to the report, some participants have already told J Camp they want to become programme leaders when they grow up. Some leaders have also taken what they learned into diversity initiatives in their workplaces and communities.J Camp expanded its efforts to include wheelchair rugby in 2025, giving participants another sporting option.In Osaka’s case, the project reflects the goal she set when she launched Play Academy: giving more girls the chance to discover what sport can offer them. Through its support for J Camp, the initiative helps create opportunities not only for girls to play, but also for young women to become role models for others.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka launched Play Academy in 2020 with Nike and Laureus Sport for Good. In Japan, that support reaches J Camp, which uses wheelchair basketball to help girls with and without disabilities take part in sport. Through Push for Future, J Camp trains young women, including those with disabilities, in areas such as safeguarding and working with children with disabilities.

Article Title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s 25-year bond transcends 30 Grand Slams as tennis icons rewrite the playbook on family healing and raising grounded children

Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a family life that goes beyond their success on the tennis court. The couple, who have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them, married on October 22, 2001, and have two children, Jaden and Jaz. As Agassi recently shared in an interview with HELLO!, their children have grown up with their own interests, away from the expectation of following their parents into tennis. Their approach to family life offers a glimpse into how two sporting champions balance fame, marriage and parenthood.Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf both reached the top of tennis after starting the sport at a young age. Agassi won eight Grand Slam singles titles, while Graf won 22. They also each won an Olympic singles gold medal, making them the only two players in tennis history to complete a Career Golden Slam.Their careers brought years of competition, public attention and demanding schedules. Agassi has spoken openly about his complicated relationship with tennis in his autobiography, Open. His experiences included intense training under his father, Mike Agassi, and leaving home as a teenager to train at Nick Bollettieri’s tennis academy in Florida.Graf also began playing tennis as a young child and went on to become one of the sport’s most successful players. Her 22 Grand Slam singles titles included four Australian Open titles, six French Open titles, seven Wimbledon titles and five US Open titles.The pair married in Las Vegas in 2001, after both had established themselves as tennis greats. Their son, Jaden, was born four days after their wedding, and their daughter, Jaz, arrived in October 2003.Agassi and Graf have not expected their children to follow them into professional tennis. Their son, Jaden, chose baseball and developed his skills as a pitcher.Jaden attended the University of Southern California, where he played for the USC Trojans baseball team. In February 2025, Major League Baseball reported that he would represent Germany in the World Baseball Classic qualifiers. The decision gave him an opportunity to pursue a sport different from the one that made his parents famous.His choice also reflects the freedom to develop an identity outside his family’s tennis history. Rather than competing on the same courts as his parents, Jaden has worked towards his own goals in baseball.Their daughter, Jaz, has pursued interests that include dance and equestrian activities. Both children have grown up with parents who understand the demands of professional sport, but their careers have taken different directions.Agassi discussed their upbringing in his September 2026 interview with HELLO! during the Laver Cup in London. He explained how their children had learned by watching their parents’ everyday behaviour and seeing how other people treated them.“They see us, they learn from what we do, not from what we say,” Agassi said.He also described their outlook on life in simple terms: “They’re shockingly balanced,” he added proudly. Yahoo SportsAgassi returned to the tennis spotlight in September 2026 as captain of Team World at the Laver Cup in London. The tournament, held at The O2 from September 25 to 27, brought him back into a team environment after his playing career.Speaking to HELLO! during the event, Agassi explained that Graf understands why tennis remains important to him, even after retirement.“She likes seeing me happy, just like I like seeing her happy,” he said.He added that she understands the value he places on the tournament and the opportunity to connect with the sport again.“She knows this is a week in Laver Cup that I value, that I bond with, that I connect to. It’s a lot of work, but she’s never been scared of me in work mode.”Agassi also joked about the need to balance his professional commitments with time away from work.“I always promised her I wouldn’t be too busy or too bored - because I’m kind of dangerous in both! She appreciates my connection to it, so she’ll smile for a week.”His comments offer a glimpse into how the couple support each other’s interests. Both know what it takes to compete at the highest level, which gives them a shared understanding of the demands that come with professional tennis.Agassi and Graf have also supported causes focused on children’s futures, with education and mental health among their areas of work.Agassi established the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education in 1994. One of its major projects was the Andre Agassi College Preparatory Academy, a public charter school that opened in Las Vegas in 2001. The school aimed to provide children in Historic West Las Vegas with a strong education and prepare them for college. Its operations were later transferred to Democracy Prep in 2017.Graf founded Children for Tomorrow in Hamburg, Germany, in 1998. The organisation supports children and young people who have experienced war, persecution and other forms of organised violence.According to the foundation’s official website, it provides medical and psychological care to affected children and supports their healthy development. The organisation is based at the University Medical Centre Hamburg-Eppendorf and works with children who need help dealing with traumatic experiences.The two initiatives focus on different needs, but both work to give children access to support and opportunities. Agassi’s project centres on education, while Graf’s foundation provides care for children affected by violence and displacement.Their work outside tennis adds another part to their public lives. Alongside their sporting records, they have supported efforts to improve children’s access to education and mental health services.After 25 years of marriage, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf continue to share a life shaped by their experiences in professional sport. Their children have followed different interests, and both parents have spoken about the importance of leading by example. Their family life and charitable work show how their interests now extend well beyond their achievements on the tennis court.
Article Summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have built a family life that goes beyond their success on the tennis court. The couple, who have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them, married on October 22, 2001, and have two children, Jaden and Jaz. Their approach to family life offers a glimpse into how two sporting champions balance fame, marriage and parenthood.

Article Title: Nike’s Mumbai Indians deal: A statement of intent in India’s growing sports market
Article Text:
Mumbai Indians have entered into a multi-year kit manufacturing deal with Nike. The partnership begins in 2027.

NEW DELHI:

Mumbai Indians head coach Kieron Pollard sports the new jersey with the Nike logo. (Image: X)

They (Nike) have obviously realised in the last few years that cricket is a sport which is important to have on the roster GroupM's Vinit Karnik

Nike were Team India's kit manufacturers from 2006 until 2020. (BCCI)

European football teams' loyal fans will buy the official jersey even if it means spending Rs 5,000-6,000. In India, the market is very different. Look at the IPL teams, how many fans will actually be able to afford a jersey worth Rs 5,000? Indranil Das Blah

Nike will become the official kit partner for Mumbai Indians’ men’s and women’s teams in India from the 2027 season under a multi-year partnership.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On October 21, Nike and Mumbai Indians (MI) entered into a multi-year partnership for the men's and women's teams, starting from 2027. MI staff are slated to sport the new gear this month, while women's and men's teams are expected to showcase it ahead of their respective seasons. This is Nike's first IPL kit deal since working with the now-defunct Deccan Chargers in 2008 - 18 years ago.What makes this partnership unique to the current kit manufacturing deals with IPL franchises is that it will see the iconic Nike Swoosh on the Mumbai Indians jerseys. In the world of shirt sponsorships, where IPL franchises such as MI, Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Chennai Super Kings demand a reported Rs 40-60 crore per season for the front jersey, it is premium retail space."The partnership marks a significant step in Nike’s continued investment in cricket and reflects the brand’s long-term commitment to athletes, fans and the future of sport in India," said the company in a press note.Before Nike, MI had Performax Activewear (2019-2024) and Skechers (2024-2026) as kit manufacturers."This is a really good opportunity for MI to continue to build on their current offering and deliver world-class merchandise to the fans.They will work with Nike’s global team, bring some interesting and exciting merchandise for fans and co-create cool collaborations that will supplement the match wear," said an industry insider."With Nike, the fabrics are going to get better, performance-wise it will get better. It will help the players also, like if you see how global football teams always put emphasis on their match jerseys, to help with performance. In the next few years, you are going to see interesting things that this partnership will bring to the MI fans," they continued.Nike has had a long-standing relationship with Indian cricket. The Oregon-headquartered company, which entered India in 2004, was the Indian men's cricket team's kit sponsor from 2006 until 2020, before being replaced by MPL Sports, Killer Jeans and then Adidas.In December 2005, Nike spent Rs 195 crore to outbid Adidas and Rebook for the national team's jersey. In 2011, after Men in Blue won the ODI World Cup, that deal value ballooned to Rs 270 crore for another five years. In 2016, Nike spent approximately Rs 370 crore on a four-and-a-half-year deal, paying Rs 87.34 lakh per match.Since 2010, value of the IPL has gone from $4.13 billion to $9.6 billion, growing 2.13-times, as per a study by Brand Finance. Why, then, did Nike stay away from the biggest sports league in the country?"These guys were brought into the IPL ecosystem way too early. That was the time when market was just maturing because merchandise etc. are pretty new to India. Indians were not used to the whole club or franchise kind of a model," explained Vinit Karnik, GroupM's Managing Director, an industry veteran of three decades."Second, Nike were Team India's principle kit sponsor and then they let that go off their hands. They have obviously realised in the last few years that cricket is a sport which is important to have on the roster.""Third, ever since those days of pre-mature or not mature enough days of Indian cricket, the amount of money an average Indian fan spends on sports merchandise is quite significant. So maybe that changes the whole business dynamics," he added.Indranil Das Blah, former Mumbai City FC CEO and now founder of AMP Sports & Entertainment, believes the last-minute modifications to the jersey doesn't help these international manufacturers."The last moment nature of the IPL that tends to happen (plays a role). So, local manufacturers can fill in that void, but international manufacturers need a lot more planning, which is why most of them disappear for the longest time from the scene," said Blah.He reckons this is also about Nike showcasing it's intent. "Globally, Nike has been struggling. But this is a statement of intent, saying India is a critical market for us. And if it is critical, you have to be in cricket. Now look at the top assets. Adidas, your biggest competitor, has the Indian cricket team. That leaves the likes of CSK and MI. So if you want to be in India and want to be visible, you can't have a better platform than MI," he added.While Nike stayed away from the IPL ecosystem, its biggest competitors remained attached to the league. Seven has been associated with Chennai Super Kings; Puma with Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Delhi Capitals; SIX5SIX with Lucknow Super Giants and Kolkata Knight Riders.Another factor that might have played a role in Nike staying away is the price. The men's cricket team jersey around the 2010s had two variants: a true replica worth Rs 3,000 and a cheaper alternative at Rs 2,000, which had inferior fabric while maintaining the visual appeal. By the time Nike exited, the replica cost nearly Rs 5,000. This was in sharp contrast to the Rs 200-300 that fans were willing to spend outside the stadiums."European football teams' loyal fans will buy the official jersey even if it means spending Rs 5,000-6,000. In India, the market is very different. Look at the IPL teams, how many fans will actually be able to afford a jersey worth Rs 5,000? In football, they have a home, away and official jersey. In India, very few people can afford that. And for these international manufacturers, it's not like they can produce cheap jerseys, right? There has to be a certain quality to that. So, your market is instantly decreased," stated Blah.For it to make business sense now, the pricing has to be reasonable, believes Karnik."India is not a premium market. You will have to create a product which is more affordable to people. And that's one of the learnings they will have from 2008. So I think when they announce the MI range, they will have multiple layers. The top product cost be worth Rs 5,000 but they will do a Rs 999 or Rs 1499 kind of range, which is more affordable."Cricket is not the only sport where Nike has had an association in India. In February 2006, Nike entered into a seven-year deal to become the official kit sponsor of the Indian football team. The terms enabled them to undertake marketing and promotional activities for them at the grassroots level.The deal with the All India Football Federation (AIFF) was extended in 2013 before SIX5SIX stepped in ahead of the 2019 AFC Asian Cup, ending a 12-year association.Back to cricket, and the IPL specifically, will this deal boost IPL's brand value? Karnik believes it is just one team and one entry point at this point. He thinks it will become big if Nike, Adidas or Puma were "across all 10 teams like in the Premier League, NBA or NFL. If that happened then that becomes significant point to make. But with one team, I don't know. Would it translate into valuation for IPL or MI? Or, both? I don't think so," he finished.
Article Summary: Mumbai Indians have entered into a multi-year kit manufacturing deal with Nike. The partnership begins in 2027. This is Nike's first IPL kit deal since working with the now-defunct Deccan Chargers in 2008 - 18 years ago. In December 2005, Nike spent Rs 195 crore to outbid Adidas and Rebook for the national team's jersey.

Article Title: Neeraj Yadav death: Friend says she met para athlete hours before he was found beside SUV
Article Text:
Neeraj Yadav (Image credit: Agencies)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Yadav , a 42-year-old three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist, was found dead beside his SUV near Maujpur metro station in northeast Delhi Monday night in a suspected case of suicide. Yadav, who hailed from UP, used to run Anshneer Sports Academy in Haryana’s Sonipat. He is survived by his wife and their three-year-old daughter.Police received information from GTB Hospital around 12.08 am Tuesday that a person had been brought to its emergency department and declared dead by the attending doctors.“A team reached Rajiv Gandhi Hospital, where the emergency services of GTB Hospital are currently being operated, and the body had already been shifted to GTB Hospital’s mortuary,” an officer said.During inquiry, a woman who had brought Yadav to the hospital told police she had been friends with him since Dec 2025. According to her statement, she went to Sonipat on Oct 27 to meet Yadav and tell him she could no longer remain in touch with him. She told police Yadav later dropped her off at Maujpur in his SUV.Around 9pm, when the woman returned to the area near Gate No. 1 of Maujpur metro station to check on him, she found him lying on the road beside his vehicle and rushed him to hospital.Jafrabad police station has begun proceedings under BNSS Section 194, which deals with police inquiries and reports in cases of suicide and other unnatural deaths. “We have not found any suicide note or video,” an officer said.Speaking to reporters, a relative of Yadav said, “He had struggled, fought his way through difficulties and continued playing. It is difficult for me to believe that he could take the extreme step.”He also said he was unaware of the woman who had accompanied Yadav before his death and called for her role to be examined.Despite being diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, Yadav pursued his sporting ambitions, playing wheelchair tennis between 2005 and 2012 before switching to para-athletics. His breakthrough came at the 2015 Delhi State Athletics Meet, where he won gold medals in the shot put, javelin and discus events.Yadav announced himself on the international stage at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, winning gold in the men’s F55 javelin throw with an Asian-record effort of 29.84 metres. He subsequently clinched two gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in 2023, winning the javelin and discus events to take his career tally to three Asian Para Games titles.However, his career was clouded by an anti-doping case. National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended him after an out-of-competition sample collected in Bengaluru in 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid. He sought DNA testing of his sample through the anti-doping disciplinary process. He was later banned for four years.India’s chief para-athletics coach S Satyanarayana suggested Yadav may have been under emotional distress after missing the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games because of his doping suspension. “Medals at the Asian Para Games can bring substantial govt cash awards. But his suspension had not ended, and he could not compete. It is possible this affected him deeply,” he said.
Article Summary: Neeraj Yadav, 42, a three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist, was found dead near Maujpur metro station in northeast Delhi Monday night. Police received information from GTB Hospital around 12.08 am Tuesday that a person had been brought to its emergency department and declared dead by the attending doctors. Police have not found any suicide note or video.

Article Title: How Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s donation helped a Nashville free grocery store resume support for families on its waitlist
Article Text:
An unexpected email

A $26 million charity donation

Pop icon Taylor Swift , 36, and NFL star Travis Kelce , 37, exchanged their wedding vows in July this year at Madison Square Garden. Ahead of their big day, the couple spent the week giving back. They donated $26 million to 20 charities, the Associated Press reported. One recipient was The Store, a Nashville non-profit fighting food insecurity. Rising food costs had forced the store to pause the admission of new families, and around 1,000 households were still waiting for help. That’s when an unexpected email arrived with a donation they simply couldn’t believe!Brittany Brown, The Store’s director of mission advancement, read the email twice before she believed it. It arrived in the days before Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in New York, a week when the couple’s names filled almost every feed. The message was not an invite. In fact, it had nothing to do with the wedding itself. It was about groceries, waiting lists and families who had been asked to be patient for months. Brown, whose job also involves explaining the non-profit’s work to donors and keeping the shelves stocked, quickly realised this was not routine support. “I quickly checked my email and was blown away, just really blown away,” Brown told Channel 5 Nashville.Country star Brad Paisley and actress Kimberly Williams-Paisley founded The Store, which opened in 2020. It works like a regular supermarket. Families referred to the store choose the food that fits their needs, with volunteers helping them shop. The store goes beyond traditional food aid and aims for longer-term solutions, according to its website.The donation arrived when The Store was struggling with rising grocery costs and had temporarily stopped accepting new families, leaving 1,000 households on its waiting list. Although Brown did not disclose the amount donated, she said the money would allow the organisation to begin admitting families again. “With this gift, we’re now going to be able to unpause that pause,” Brown told the broadcaster.In a video shared on Instagram, Brad Paisley called the donation ‘transformative’. “We just wanted to take a second and say it’s transformative, it will feed so many families, and what a way to start a marriage. I’m so excited,” the country star said.Kimberly said they were “so, so grateful”. She also pointed out that food insecurity was at a 10-year high in the Nashville area, making the timing “just so critical”. She added, “We’re just really grateful for your generosity.”Brown agreed: “What a wonderful thing to be thinking of others during such a chaotic time of wedding planning.”The gift was part of a larger round of giving. Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce made donations totalling $26 million to charities ahead of their wedding day. The donations were spread across 20 local and national charities, according to Swift’s publicist, with many located in areas where the couple has deep ties, the AP reported. Nine of these were based in New York, ranging from the Food Bank For NYC and City Harvest to Musical Mentors, a non-profit that connects music teachers with students in need.The couple’s ties to Nashville are evident in their generous donation. The pop star has called Nashville one of her homes since she was a teenager. However, her gift to The Store is particularly close to her heart because of her relationship with the Paisleys. In 2007, when Swift was just 17 and promoting her debut album, she opened for Brad Paisley on his Bonfires and Amplifiers Tour. Nearly two decades later, the friendship remains strong. In fact, the Paisleys attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding.
Article Summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to 20 charities. One recipient was The Store, a Nashville non-profit fighting food insecurity. Rising food costs had forced the store to pause the admission of new families. Around 1,000 households were still waiting for help.

Article Title: NFL Trade Rumor: $62M Indianapolis Colts RB linked to Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos
Article Text:

Jonathan Taylor contract with Indianapolis Colts

Jonathan Taylor’s wife Ayanna Chapman worries her husband may be traded from the Indianapolis Colts. Because two players were traded after Week 7 loss and a general manager was fired after a Week 6 loss.Jonathan Taylor is one of the potential trade candidates. He is a valuable veteran who may be on the rival teams’ radars before the November 10 trade deadline. But before we take his wife Ayanna Chapman’s worries seriously, a NFL insider spilled the beans on the trade rumors.ESPN insider Adam Schefter said he understood that Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon would not be willing to trade Jonathan Taylor. 'The Colts could retain the running back unless its stance changed. “The big name is Jonathan Taylor. My understanding is that the owner doesn’t want to trade Jonathan Taylor,” Adam Schefter told Pat McAfee.NFL insider Adam Schefter believes the Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s Indianapolis Colts are unlikely to trade Jonathan Taylor before the NFL trade deadline. Even if other teams are interested.The Colts may be denying it right now only to drive up the trade price. “We have two weeks from now until the deadline,” Schefter told Pat McAfee on The Pat McAfee Show.“I’m sure they don’t want to trade Jonathan Taylor. And if I had to guess today, I don’t think they will trade Jonathan Taylor. But I think there are going to be teams that are interested out there that will try to have conversations, make offers.And if the Colts don’t change their stance, they won’t trade Jonathan Taylor. But again, I think the owner doesn’t want to trade him for the record right now. Now that doesn’t mean it won’t happen. By the way, that may just be their stance to drive up the price.”Pat McAfee agreed that the franchise could be playing poker to drive up Taylor’s trade value. McAfee also praised Taylor as one of the league’s best running backs.“Yeah, this could be poker. But on that note, Jonathan Taylor is by far one of the best running backs in the league. There is no question about it,” McAfee told Schefter.Jonathan Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August 2026. The deal includes a $15 million signing bonus, $39.02 million in guaranteed money, and a $22 million average annual income.In 2026, he is scheduled to earn a $6.98 million base salary, a $15 million signing bonus, and a $5,440 workout bonus, with a $16.19 million cap hit and $25.56 million in dead cap value. His total career earnings are $62 million over 7 NFL seasons, including 2026.Trading Taylor could be a significant financial decision for the franchise. His contract and production will attract contenders; however, interest alone doesn’t guarantee a deal.Indianapolis Colts owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon must deem the transaction fit. She may not want the Sauce Gardner mistake to be repeated. Still, if teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old running back, here are his landing spots.According to a report mentioned by NBC Sports’ Mike Florio, the Minnesota Vikings, Denver Broncos, Seattle Seahawks, and the Green Bay Packers have been linked to the Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.Pro Football Talk host Mike Florio thought the report mentioned the Packers as an odd choice because they got Josh Jacobs back. The analyst doesn’t think Green Bay will be trading for Taylor.It won’t be the Seahawks because they’ve already done business with them - Quenton Nelson. It could be the Vikings and the Broncos.Denver could be objectively looking at RJ Harvey and JK Dobbins, thinking, ’These guys are good, but they are not great.’ Jonathan Taylor could help push Denver’s offense where it needs to go. The passing game isn’t where it needs to be, and quarterback Bo Nix is still trying to find his footing.PFT Live co-host Chris Simms agrees with Mike Florio that the Broncos are the second-best landing spot for Jonathan Taylor. So, who’s it going to be? The Denver Broncos or the Minnesota Vikings.The Vikings seem to have their own show going with six straight wins. The Broncos might need a little push to go from good to great. So, would Ayanna Chapman’s worries come true? Only time will tell us that.
