Article Title: Congress opens account in MLC polls as Abhijit Wanjari retains Nagpur seat after nail-biting contest
Article Text:
Image Credit: ANI (Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes)





NAGPUR: Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat, ending a contest that saw the lead change hands during more than 40 hours of counting.Wanjari secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960.The result came after Kohale, a former MLA, had taken a lead of 4,294 votes over Wanjari after the second round of counting on Wednesday.Kohale had polled 60,924 first-preference votes, against Wanjari's 56,630. Independent candidate Nitesh Karale received 24,249 votes.With no candidate securing the required quota on first-preference votes, the counting proceeded to second-preference votes. Wanjari eventually overtook Kohale in the elimination rounds, a senior poll official told news agency PTI.The contest was closely watched as Nagpur is the home turf of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari , both of whom had campaigned extensively for Kohale.The Nagpur graduates' seat had been represented for several terms by Gadkari, who served as an MLC before entering national politics.Wanjari had defeated BJP candidate Sandip Joshi in the previous election.Before the final result was declared, Kohale questioned the effectiveness of the voting process in graduates' and teachers' constituencies, while indicating that he would accept the outcome.“Going by the trends in the last few rounds, it appears that the result may tilt in favour of the Congress candidate. Whatever the result, I am ready to accept it.”The Maharashtra legislative council elections were held for five constituencies, with the Mahayuti and the Maha Vikas Aghadi winning two seats each. The results also exposed differences within the ruling Mahayuti alliance of the BJP, Shiv Sena and NCP, which failed to secure a uniform victory across the contests.The BJP won one seat and its ally Shiv Sena another, while the Ajit Pawar-led NCP failed to win any. The Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) secured two seats, benefiting from disagreements among Mahayuti partners over seat-sharing.
Article Summary: Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat.Wanjari secured 67,231 votes against Kohale's 63,960. The result came after Kohale, a former MLA, had taken a lead of 4,294 votes.

Article Title: Bengaluru man calls date to friend’s home, 2 transgender persons rob 226g gold
Article Text:
(AI Image) 42-year-old Rohith realized his valuables had been stolen after granting access to his friend Thilak, who was then threatened by armed intruders.





BENGALURU: Lending a friend his house keys for a day turned into an expensive mistake for a 42-year-old man, who returned to find his cupboard broken open and 226 grams of gold jewellery missing. His friend, who had invited a stranger he met on a dating app to the house, was allegedly threatened at knifepoint by two people who ransacked the bedroom and fled with the valuables.According to the complaint filed by Rohith (name changed), a private firm employee and resident of Nagarabhavi, he had been living with his family in a rented house for seven years. On Oct 21, his wife left for Tamil Nadu on a trip. The following afternoon, Rohith went to his house in Hesaraghatta, leaving the keys with his friend Thilak (name changed), who had asked to stay there for a day.Thilak reached the house around 7.30pm on Oct 22.Thilak had struck up a conversation with a match on Grindr, a dating app used by the LGBTQA+ community, and invited someone he believed was a woman to the house. The visitor arrived around 10.15pm wearing a face mask. After removing it, the person was identified by Thilak as a transgender, according to his account.The two chatted for some time. Soon, the visitor walked into a room and began checking the cupboard.When Thilak questioned the person, the visitor allegedly threatened him, warning him to keep quiet.The visitor also threatened to call others. Thilak, worried that a commotion in the neighbourhood would land him in trouble, asked the visitor to leave. Instead, the visitor made a phone call and, about 10 minutes later, another person arrived at the house.The duo allegedly made Thilak sit in the hall, with one of them standing guard and brandishing a knife to keep him from raising an alarm. The other broke open the almirah and took away the jewellery. Before fleeing, the two allegedly pushed Thilak aside.Around 11.45pm, Thilak called Rohith, who rushed back to the house around 12.30am. A check revealed that a mangalya chain, a necklace, bangles, three gold chains, a bracelet, a maati, five rings and three pairs of earrings were missing, weighing approximately 226 grams in total.Rohith lodged a complaint with Chandra Layout police. Police have registered a case under BNS Section 309 for robbery and are making efforts to trace the accused.
Article Summary: 42-year-old Rohith left his house keys with his friend Thilak for a day. He returned to find his cupboard broken and 226 grams of gold jewellery missing. His friend, who had invited a stranger he met on a dating app to the house, was allegedly threatened at knifepoint by two people who ransacked the bedroom.

Article Title: Maharashtra MLC polls: Mahayuti wins 2 seats, NCP-SP clinches 2 for MVA
Article Text:
BJP's Kaustubh Gawade with supporters after winning Pune seat on Wednesday

Polling in other states

Cracks within partners cost Mahayuti

Why counting takes time

Boost for NCP (SP), introspection for allies

‘Wake-up call’ for NCP: Praful Patel

(With inputs from Vaibhav Ganjapure and Abhishek Choudhari in Nagpur)





PUNE: Mahayuti and MVA won two seats each across the five graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies in Maharashtra legislative council elections, while the Nagpur graduates’ constituency emerged as the most dramatic contest, with the result hanging in the balance at the time of going to the press even though Congress claimed victory.The overall results exposed fault lines within the BJP-Shiv Sena-NCP Mahayuti, which failed to function as a cohesive alliance across the five constituencies.While BJP secured one seat, its partner Sena bagged another and NCP didn’t win any.Despite entering the polls as favourites, Mahayuti partners were mired in disagreements over seat-sharing, creating openings that Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) successfully exploited to secure two key contests.In a cliffhanger at Nagpur’s Mankapur Sports Complex, BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale and Congress candidate Abhijit Wanjarri traded leads through the day as counting stretched beyond 40 hours.Wanjarri surged ahead in the initial rounds before Kohale clawed his way back. With successive rounds narrowing the gap, both camps remained on edge as the final count progressed.The contest carried significance beyond a single seat. For BJP, it was a chance to reclaim a constituency it had dominated since the Jan Sangh era.For Congress, retaining the seat would reinforce its 2020 breakthrough, when Wanjarri defeated BJP’s Sandip Joshi. The battle was widely seen as a test of organisational strength in a region long regarded as a BJP bastion.Even before the final result, Kohale signalled acceptance of a possible defeat.Questioning the effectiveness of the voting process in graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, he said, “Going by the trends in the last few rounds, it appears that the result may tilt in favour of the Congress candidate. Whatever the result, I am ready to accept it and will continue to carry out whatever responsibilities my party assigns to me.”Maharashtra Congress took a dig at chief minister Devendra Fadnavis over the Nagpur MLC seat, claiming that he had to delete a post from his own X account, in which he had stated that the Congress had won “zero” seats.“Devendraji posted a message in such haste that he later had to delete it. But remember, you can delete a tweet, not the truth,” the state Congress said in a post on its official X account.Among Mahayuti’s victories, BJP’s Kaustubh Gawade won the Pune teachers’ constituency, defeating Shiv Sena rebel Sachin Sanap. In Amravati teachers’ constituency, Shiv Sena’s Kiran Sarnaik overcame Congress candidate Aditi Pohare and Sena rebel Shrikant Deshpande.The MVA’s victories came through NCP (SP). Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav won the Pune graduates’ seat by defeating BJP’s Smita Jadhav, while Pratapsinh Patil unseated three-term MLC Satish Chavan in the Aurangabad graduates’ constituency.Political analyst Prakash Pawar said the outcome reflected BJP’s miscalculation during seat-sharing talks.“The election results revealed that even though BJP remains the most dominant party in the state, it has yet to secure organic support across all sections of society. The party tried to use its dominance to dictate seat-sharing arrangements and contest the polls without the support of its alliance partners but failed to garner sufficient support. It will have to rework its strategy in the state before facing the next elections,” he said.Senior BJP leader and cabinet minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule rejected suggestions that the results represented a setback. “The five seats were previously held by opposition parties, and we had no seats. Unlike the opposition parties, whenever we face a setback, we introspect and rework our strategy to win next time,” he said.Observers pointed particularly to western Maharashtra, where Mahayuti’s seat-sharing formula left NCP with no constituency to contest in the Pune division.“NCP has traditionally been strong there, but Mahayuti gave Sunetra Pawar’s NCP no seats in the Pune division, with both constituencies going to BJP. As a result, NCP workers did not campaign actively for Mahayuti candidates and were disappointed that their party did not get a ticket,” political analyst Pawar said.Shiv Sena workers were also conspicuously absent from BJP’s Pune campaign. Chief minister Eknath Shinde-led Sena even backed rebel candidates contesting against BJP-supported nominees in the teachers’ constituency.Former MLA and Shiv Sena’s Pune chief Ravindra Dhangekar raised concerns over the role of money in the elections.“We suspect that money power played a dominant role in the elections, which is quite unfortunate. In elections to graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies, we expect deserving candidates to be given tickets. Unfortunately, political parties have taken centre stage instead of the candidates, which is wrong,” he said.NCP (SP) state president Shashikant Shinde described the outcome as a morale booster.“The election results will be a turning point for our party, as they will send positive signals to our party workers ahead of the next elections. The results also underline the fact that when qualified candidates are nominated, voters support them,” he said.At the same time, he admitted that better coordination within the opposition alliance could have yielded more victories.“We should have started coordinating with our alliance partners much earlier for these elections, and we could have won more seats. The lack of coordination has cost us some seats,” he said.State Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal said his party had fought hard in the constituencies it contested and flagged the issue of invalid votes.“Our party contested three seats and made every effort to win. The counting process revealed that a large number of votes were declared invalid, which is a matter of concern,” he said.The verdict also triggered soul-searching within NCP after the defeat of senior leader Satish Chavan in the Aurangabad graduates’ constituency.NCP working president Praful Patel termed the result a warning signal and called for sweeping organisational reforms. In a social media post, Patel said: “The election results serve as a definitive wake-up call. The time has come for urgent introspection to rebuild trust, realign our priorities and fix our organisational structure. To regain people’s trust, reset the party’s priorities and bring about organisational reforms, an immediate and rigorous self-examination will be necessary. ”
Article Summary: Mahayuti and MVA won two seats each across the five graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies in Maharashtra legislative council elections. Results exposed fault lines within the BJP-Shiv Sena-NCP Mahayuti, which failed to function as a cohesive alliance.

LUCKNOW: In a closely fought contest, the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party ended the Legislative Council elections with a 6-5 scoreline for 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. Results for all six Teachers’ constituencies and four of five Graduates’ constituencies had been declared by late Wednesday. The SP candidate had an unassailable lead in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency. The party also retained the Teachers' seat of the district.Of the six Teachers’ seats, BJP won four while the SP secured two. In the Graduates’ constituencies, BJP has won two seats and the SP three. BJP has retained five out of the six seats it had won in 2020, lost one and gained one seat. SP, on the other hand, retained its tally of three seats of 2020 and gained two new seats.Of the 11 seats, six — Lucknow Graduates', Lucknow Teachers', Meerut Graduates', Meerut Teachers', Agra Graduates' and Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' — were held by BJP in 2020. The SP candidates won three seats: Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates', Varanasi Graduates and Varanasi Teachers.Independent MLCs Dhruv Tripathi and Akash Agarwal won the remaining two seats — Teachers’ seats in Gorakhpur-Faizabad and Agra.However, Tripathi later joined the BJP, while Agarwal joined the SP just before the poll and entered the 2026 electoral contest as the party’s official candidate.This time, Tripathi won the closest contest of these polls in the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachers’ constituency, defeating Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav by a narrow margin of 307 votes.Tripathi secured 16,790 votes, with the outcome decided after counting of second-preference votes. This was his fourth consecutive win. He had won as an independent on the previous three occasions.Following his victory, Tripathi acknowledged the tough competition posed by his rival and praised Rajiv Yadav for putting up a strong fight and winning the confidence of teachers.He said victory and defeat are part of the electoral process, but ultimately a win remains a win. Kanti received 56,905 votes, while BJP’s Avnish secured 39,778 votes. Kanti had won the seat as an independent in 2014 but lost to Avnish in 2020.In the Varanasi Graduates’ constituency, SP’s Ashutosh Sinha took a decisive lead over BJP’s Kedar Nath Singh as the final preferential vote rounds concluded. After the 4th round of voting, Sinha secured 22,599 preferential votes against Singh’s 15,404 votes, opening up a commanding lead of 7,195 votes.In the Meerut Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate Dinesh Kumar Goyal emerged victorious by approximately 13,000 votes against SP’s Paremendra Singh, while party colleague Manvendra Pratap Singh won the Agra Graduates’ seat against SP’s Shashank Yadav by a margin of8,856 votes. BJP had won both the seats in 2020.SP retained the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates’ constituency, where Maan Singh Yadav defeated BJP’sAshok Kumar Rathaur by a margin of27,663 votes.Among the Teachers’ constituencies, BJP candidate Umesh Dwivedi won the Lucknow seat defeating SP’s Sushil Kumar by4,808 votes,while SP candidate Lal Bihari Yadav retained Varanasi, overwhelming BJP’s Pramod Mishra by4,898 votes.Shrichand Sharma won the Meerut seat against SP’sNitin Tomar by13,241 votes, while Hari Singh Dhillon retained the Bareilly-Moradabad seat, defeating SP’s Danish Akhtar by17,676 votes.

Article Title: Sam Altman is 'unhappy' with most MBA students; that he calls his 'chronic disappointment'; says: They always want to go do the thing that ...
Article Text:
'They always want to do the thing that was cool five years ago'

Sam Altman: AI creating a new generation of companies

A founder’s perspective

Other tech leaders share similar views

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has criticised what he sees as the tendency of many MBA graduates to pursue yesterday’s trends instead of embracing new opportunities created by artificial intelligence, calling it his ‘chronic disappointment’ with business school students. According to a report by Fortune, speaking during an interview with Stanford Graduate School of Business, Altman said AI is set to transform large parts of the job market, but argued that the disruption will also create unprecedented opportunities for ambitious workers and entrepreneurs willing to think differently. "It's totally true that huge numbers of tasks that people do today will be done better, cheaper, and faster by AI - and completely differently," Altman said, adding that wide swaths of existing jobs could eventually be handled by AI technologies. The transition, however, is likely to take time rather than happen overnight, according to the OpenAI chief.Altman reserved some of his sharpest comments for MBA students, arguing that many focus on following established career paths rather than exploring emerging opportunities. "My chronic disappointment with MBA students is that they always want to go do the thing that was cool five years ago rather than try something new," Altman said."I think this is a great time to go do the new thing."The comments come at a time when AI is reshaping industries ranging from software development and customer service to healthcare, finance and education, creating uncertainty over future job roles while simultaneously opening new business opportunities.According to Altman, AI is creating conditions for entrepreneurs to build companies that would have been difficult or impossible to launch just a few years ago. "There are many companies that can be built on top of the technology OpenAI has put out into the world that will be much bigger and, I hope, more important than OpenAI," he said. The executive pointed to periods of significant technological change as being among the best times for ambitious individuals to start careers or launch ventures."If you're heading into the world right now to work on something, I think you want to start your career at a time of the greatest change, when the playing field is most open," Altman said. He added that people with strong ideas, new skills and unconventional ways of looking at problems often perform best when industries are undergoing major shifts.Altman has built companies from scratch. He dropped out of Stanford, where he studied computer science, in 2005 to co-found the location-based social networking start-up Loopt, which was later acquired. He then joined the start-up accelerator Y Combinator and served as its president from 2014 to 2019. He now sees AI as a chance for a new generation of founders to tackle problems that once seemed out of reach.Altman's optimism about AI-driven entrepreneurship is shared by other technology leaders. Alexis Ohanian, co-founder of Reddit, has argued that startups created in the AI era have an inherent advantage because they are designed around the technology from the beginning rather than retrofitting it into existing business models. Meanwhile, billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban has repeatedly urged founders to view AI as a core business capability rather than an optional tool. "If you're not using AI to move faster or make smarter decisions, you're behind," Cuban previously told Fortune.
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman criticises MBA graduates for pursuing yesterday's trends instead of embracing new opportunities created by artificial intelligence. Altman: 'My chronic disappointment with MBA students is that they always want to go do the thing that was cool five years ago rather than try something new' Comments come at a time when AI is reshaping industries ranging from software development to healthcare.

Article Title: World Psoriasis Day: Is psoriasis contagious? Expert explains symptoms, health risks and new treatment
Article Text:
Is psoriasis contagious? What a dermatologist wants people to know

Why does psoriasis cause red, scaly patches?

Psoriasis is not always just a skin problem

Can psoriasis be treated? What newer medicines can do

When should you see a dermatologist?

A red, scaly patch on the elbow. Flakes along the hairline. Dry, irritated skin that keeps coming back. For someone with psoriasis, these symptoms can be uncomfortable enough without having to deal with another problem: people assuming they can catch it.That fear can change how others behave. Someone may hesitate before shaking hands, sharing a towel or sitting close to a person whose skin looks inflamed. But psoriasis does not spread through touch, and people living with the condition pose no risk to those around them. The patches may be visible, but what causes them has little to do with an infection.On World Psoriasis Day, it is worth looking beyond the skin itself. Psoriasis is a long-term condition linked to the immune system. It can affect a person's comfort, confidence and, in some cases, their joints and overall health. Treatments have also advanced, giving many patients more options to control symptoms than they had in the past.No, psoriasis is not contagious. You cannot catch it by touching someone's skin, sharing everyday items or spending time in the same room. It is not caused by an infection that passes from one person to another.Dr Rinky Kapoor, Co-Founder and Director of The Esthetic Clinics, says the misunderstanding can add to the difficulties faced by people with psoriasis. The condition often causes red, raised patches covered with silvery scales, and these visible signs can lead others to make assumptions about the person's health.“Psoriasis is not contagious and cannot be passed on through touch or by sharing everyday items,” Dr Kapoor explains.The confusion is understandable, but the consequences can be hurtful. People may feel the need to cover their skin, avoid social situations or explain their condition repeatedly. Someone already dealing with itching or soreness should not also have to reassure others that ordinary contact is safe.The problem begins with the immune system. In psoriasis, immune activity speeds up the growth and replacement of skin cells. These cells build up on the surface rather than shedding at their usual pace, leaving thickened patches that may itch, crack or become painful.The scalp, elbows and knees are common sites, but psoriasis can appear on the hands, feet, trunk and other parts of the body. Some people have only a few small patches. Others develop more widespread symptoms, with flare-ups that can be difficult to manage.Genes can influence a person's likelihood of developing psoriasis. Certain infections, skin injuries, stress and some medicines may trigger or worsen symptoms in people who are susceptible. But these triggers do not make psoriasis contagious.The condition can also behave differently from one person to another. Symptoms may improve for a period and then return. That does not necessarily mean a person has done something wrong or that their psoriasis is spreading to others.The World Health Organization's 2016 global report estimated that at least 100 million people worldwide were affected. Other commonly cited estimates put the number at around 125 million, or roughly 2% to 3% of the global population.That is why public awareness matters. Knowing that psoriasis cannot be passed on through contact is a simple but meaningful way to reduce the stigma surrounding it.Psoriasis is associated with psoriatic arthritis, an inflammatory condition that can cause painful, swollen or stiff joints.Joint symptoms deserve attention, particularly when they occur alongside skin flare-ups. Persistent stiffness, swelling or pain should not simply be put down to ageing or everyday aches. A doctor can assess the symptoms and determine whether further investigation or treatment is needed.Psoriasis has also been linked with other health concerns, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes and depression. These associations do not mean that everyone with psoriasis will develop these conditions. They do, however, show why ongoing medical care matters and why psoriasis should not be dismissed as a cosmetic issue.There is no permanent cure for psoriasis at present, but treatment can reduce inflammation, ease itching and help keep flare-ups under control. Depending on how severe the condition is and which areas are affected, a dermatologist may recommend creams or ointments, phototherapy, oral medicines or injectable treatments.Dr Kapoor says biological therapies have expanded the options available to people with moderate to severe psoriasis. These medicines target specific parts of the immune system involved in inflammation and can bring substantial improvement for many suitable patients.“Newer therapies like biologicals are a blessing for psoriasis patients,” she says.Some biologics can clear the skin significantly, while certain medicines can also help treat psoriatic arthritis. The results are not identical for everyone, and these treatments are not appropriate for every patient. Doctors consider the severity of the disease, other health conditions and previous treatment responses before deciding what to prescribe.Biologics also require medical supervision. Patients may need screening for certain infections before treatment and monitoring while taking the medicine. They should not start or stop treatment on their own, even if their symptoms improve.For anyone who has been struggling with recurring patches, a dermatologist can explain which treatments are available and what kind of improvement is realistic.Redness, scaling or itching that persists, keeps returning or spreads across the skin should be checked by a dermatologist. It is especially important to seek advice if the symptoms are painful or if joint pain, swelling or stiffness develops alongside them.Not every scaly patch is psoriasis. Eczema and other skin conditions can look similar, but their causes and treatments may differ. Getting the right diagnosis is better than relying on online pictures or trying several products without medical advice.The message this World Psoriasis Day is straightforward: psoriasis can be difficult to live with, but it cannot be caught from another person. A little knowledge can prevent a great deal of unnecessary discomfort. And with appropriate treatment and follow-up, many people can manage their symptoms and get on with everyday life without allowing the condition to define it.
Article Summary: On World Psoriasis Day, it is worth looking beyond the skin itself. psoriasis is a long-term condition linked to the immune system. It can affect a person's comfort, confidence and, in some cases, their joints. Treatments have advanced, giving many patients more options to control symptoms.

Article Title: The dilemma around Diwali parties – too many invites, too many people to please
Article Text:
This is the week when everyone seems to have packed evenings, with some or the other Diwali party to attend





Where to be and for how long? This dilemma of handling multiple Diwali party invites is more complicated than it sounds. And it gets even worse if you claim to have a big social circle in Delhi. This is the week when everyone seems to have packed evenings, with some or the other Diwali party to attend. From intimate house parties and family gatherings to gala dinners and grand card parties, there is quite a range to choose from. And while getting invited to all these parties might sound like a good problem to have, managing the invitations is an entirely different story. Too many invites, too little time, and the complicated business of keeping everyone happy!There are lists being drawn and calendars being marked to ensure that every invite is listed, carefully evaluated, discussed and slotted under ‘what can be missed’ and ‘what cannot’. Now, this categorisation is not as simple as choosing which party promises better food, music or company. There is the relationship with the host to consider, the location of the party, the guest list and, most importantly, the amount of damage control that might be required if you don’t show up. Some invitations can be politely declined, while others come with the risk of being reminded of your absence at every subsequent social gathering.And then there are those parties where the host has already announced to everyone that you are coming, even before you have confirmed.Once that categorisation is done, comes the other important question: How long should one stay at each party? Those where one can simply show up, pose for pictures with the hosts, exchange festive greetings and leave are the ones that come first in the order of parties to attend on a given evening. After all, photographic evidence of your attendance is sometimes just as important as attendance itself. Those where networking is involved, card games are planned or live music is part of the entertainment come later in the list. The challenge is to spend just enough time at each party to make your presence felt, without making your exit look like an escape. The fact also remains that no amount of planning can account for a party that turns out to be more entertaining than expected. What was supposed to be a quick appearance can turn into a long evening, particularly when the card games get interesting or you run into friends you haven’t met in months.And then there is the small matter of Delhi’s traffic situation. A party in Chhatarpur, another in Vasant Vihar and a third in Gurgaon might all sound manageable until you are sitting in traffic, dressed in your festive best. That’s when you begin questioning your social ambitions.While considering and making this elaborate plan of party hopping, what is also essential is the dress code. One wouldn’t want to repeat outfits at parties with common guests. So, no matter the distance or duration, some even travel with an extra change of clothes for the evening as they switch from one party to another. After all, you cannot possibly appear in the same outfit in pictures from three different parties on the same night, particularly when those pictures are likely to land on social media before you reach home.Another complication is the overlapping guest list. Delhi’s social circles might appear large, but somehow the same faces turn up at every second party. Which means the carefully planned excuse of having another commitment doesn’t always work when you run into the same people at your next stop.By the end of the festive week, the bigger achievement isn’t how many parties you attended, but how many hosts you managed to keep happy. And just when you think you have successfully navigated the Diwali social calendar, someone asks the most dreaded question, “You didn’t come to our party?” Celebrating Diwali in Delhi is one thing; navigating the party circuit is quite another. Between managing expectations and making sure nobody feels left out, the festive season can become a social balancing act.
Article Summary: This is the week when everyone seems to have packed evenings, with some or the other Diwali party to attend. From intimate house parties and family gatherings to gala dinners and grand card parties, there is quite a range to choose from. The festive season can become a social balancing act.

Article Title: Theatre review: When small-town charm overstays its welcome
Article Text:
A still from the play

Malgudi Days

Want us to review your play? Mail us at tims.delhitimes@timesofindia.com





A lone bicycle tyre rolls onto the stage. Harmoniums strike up a tune, and buyers and sellers in bright clothes begin filing one after another. Suddenly we are transported to Ramnagar of the 1970s. Hawkers speak in a lilting regional dialect, their voices occasionally chiming in with a chorus of “hegas.”The opening segment is easily one of the strongest parts of the play Lapoojhanna, set in Ramnagar, Uttarakhand, which was formerly a part of Uttar Pradesh. The enunciation of the characters, the clothes from the era, and the lovely singing to go with it all immediately evoke nostalgia.In another scene, a young love blossoms between Ashok – a new lad who has come to town with his family – and Sakina, a local girl. Sparks fly and so do chappals, as Ashok dreams up the entire romance, only for it to end with him getting a spanking from his father. Another episode sees the play’s central character, Lafttu, spending money he has stolen from his father on his friends. Comedy ensues as a raging father plays a cat-and-mouse game with his son.Portions of the play capture the small-town charm of Ramnagar, especially the scene when guests come to visit Ashok and his parents, and the children are asked to “perform” in order to entertain them.Later, Ashok and Lafftu get invited to a birthday party they had little hopes of attending. Their hesitation over presenting the gifts to the girls, given the smaller size of their parcels, highlights the insecurities that even children are not shielded from.Gaurav Kumar, who played Lafttu, is magnetic and mischievous as the naughty boy from the school. The artiste portrayed the character’s innocence and his more playful side with equal conviction.The influence of RK Narayan’sis also quite evident, notably in director Anuranjan Sharma’s staging of the battle between the unrelenting master and his students. The actors’ convincing use of body language makes for a few genuine rounds of laughter.The ending, however, is dragged out. The play could have been tighter and pacier had the last 20 minutes been chopped.-Anvita Singh
Article Summary: The opening segment is easily one of the strongest parts of the play Lapoojhanna, set in Ramnagar, Uttarakhand. The influence of RK Narayan’sis also quite evident, notably in director Anuranjan Sharma’s staging of the battle between the unrelenting master and his students.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova at Pan Pacific Open in Japan
Article Text:
Mia Pohankova and Naomi Osaka (Image credit: Reuters)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Parks, Fernandez advance

Injuries force two withdrawals

Naomi Osaka's run at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo came to an end on Thursday after she suffered a surprise defeat against Slovakia's Mia Pohankova.The seventh-seeded Osaka, playing in front of her home fans, lost 6-3, 7-5 to the 18-year-old wildcard entrant. The match lasted one hour and 35 minutes, with Pohankova booking her place in the quarterfinals.Pohankova turned 18 just a week ago. She will next face Alycia Parks for a place in the semifinals. The Slovakian made a name for herself in junior tennis by winning the girls' singles title at Wimbledon in 2025.Osaka had entered the second round on the back of a win over Jasmine Paolini in Tokyo. However, she could not continue her run against the young Slovakian.Parks also secured a place in the quarterfinals on Thursday, defeating Australia's Kimberly Birrell 6-3, 6-1.Canada's Leylah Fernandez produced another strong performance, beating fifth seed Elise Mertens 6-2, 7-6 (8) to move into the next round.In a late match, top seed Elena Rybakina was scheduled to face Yulia Putintseva. Both players were born in Russia but represent Kazakhstan.The tournament had already lost two seeded players due to injuries.Second seed Maja Chwalinska withdrew with an injury to her left thigh, while fourth seed Belinda Bencic pulled out because of a right ankle injury.
Article Summary: Mia Pohankova beats Naomi Osaka 6-3, 7-5 in one hour and 35 minutes. The 18-year-old Slovakian will next face Alycia Parks in the quarterfinals. Canada's Leylah Fernandez beats Elise Mertens in straight sets. Top seed Elena Rybakina faces Yulia Putintseva.

Article Title: Mumbai road rage: 3 men chase CA student's car, smash window with stones after near collision
Article Text:
(AI-Image) After a near-collision, the men pelted the students' car with stones, causing damage





MUMBAI: Three scooter-borne men allegedly chased a 23-year-old chartered accountancy student and his two friends through Bandra (West), pelted their car with stones and damaged it after a near-collision on Monday night. One of the occupants sustained a minor injury in the road-rage incident.Bandra resident Yuvraj Bhandari, who was driving the car, and his friends Tanishq Sawant and Aarav Lasrado, all 23, had questioned the trio after their scooter allegedly approached the car from the wrong direction at a junction. The men allegedly abused and threatened them before fleeing.Bandra police registered an FIR on Tuesday and are examining CCTV footage to identify the accused."We are trying to enhance the CCTV images for a clearer view. The trio took narrow lanes to escape, and the scooter had no visible registration number, delaying efforts to trace them. Our team is examining footage to track their escape route," a Bandra police officer said.Bhandari was driving his uncle Hitendra Bhandari's Toyota Glanza from Dr Ambedkar Road towards Carter Road around 8.45pm when the incident occurred."The three men riding a scooter in the wrong direction nearly collided head-on with our car at the Peri Road-Turner Road junction. When we questioned them, they allegedly got angry and chased us towards Khar Danda via Carter Road," Bhandari told TOI.The trio allegedly pelted the car with stones and tried to obstruct it as Bhandari drove through narrow lanes to escape. When the car later stopped at a traffic signal at the same junction, the men allegedly smashed its rear-right window and damaged the rear-right door and indicator with stones.Sawant suffered a minor injury to a finger on his right hand from broken glass and stones. The damage to the car was estimated at Rs 1 lakh.The suspects were described as slender and around 20 years old. One was wearing a white shirt and the other two black shirts.The trio has been booked under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for causing hurt, wrongful restraint, mischief causing property damage, insult, criminal intimidation and common intention.
Article Summary: Three scooter-borne men allegedly chased a 23-year-old chartered accountancy student and his two friends through Bandra (West) They pelted their car with stones and damaged it after a near-collision on Monday night. One of the occupants sustained a minor injury.

Article Title: ​NCP (SP) candidate nears Aurangabad graduate poll win; anti-incumbency, spirited campaign by rival camp hit NCP
Article Text:
NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil (centre) with supporters at the counting centre on Wednesday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil moved closer to victory in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election on Wednesday, opening a sizeable lead over NCP’s three-term MLC Satish Chavan as counting continued on the second day.With counting of ballot papers still underway late on Wednesday, Patil had secured 73,931 first-preference votes, ahead of Chavan’s 60,768. The victory quota was fixed at 88,558 votes, forcing the contest into the second-preference count as no candidate crossed the required mark.Though the final result was awaited, NCP (SP) workers began celebrations, treating Patil’s lead as decisive.“This victory is not mine alone. This victory belongs to every graduate who showed faith in me to ask the questions of our future, to fight for our rights, and to usher in a new era of education, employment, and development. This victory belongs to that youth whose eyes hold dreams, to those students who seek quality education and employment opportunities, as well as to all teachers, educated citizens, and every individual who harbors the expectation of change,” Patil said.Political observers attributed Chavan’s likely defeat to strong anti-incumbency and an aggressive campaign by NCP (SP). Several graduate voters had expressed dissatisfaction over Chavan’s alleged lack of accessibility and silence on key issues.His perceived overconfidence and strained relations with sections of Mahayuti politicians were also cited as factors.Shiv Sena MLA Abdul Sattar openly campaigned against Chavan, while some disgruntled BJP and Mahayuti functionaries were believed to have tacitly backed Patil.Patil, meanwhile, ran a tightly coordinated campaign with support from his brother, Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Rahul Patil, and senior NCP (SP) netas including Supriya Sule , Rohit Pawar, Rajesh Tope and Shashikant Shinde. His campaign focused on issues such as unemployment among graduates, contractual teachers and health insurance, while avoiding personal attacks on rivals.Among the 41 candidates in the fray, independent reel-star Raviraj Sabale finished third with more than 19,000 first-preference votes.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil moved closer to victory in the Aurangabad Graduate constituency election on Wednesday. Patil had secured 73,931 first- preference votes, ahead of Satish Chavan’s 60,768.

Article Title: High invalid votes from graduates is yet another stark story of MLC polls, tradition continues
Article Text:
Kolhapur:

Scribblings on ballot papers steal the show





The graduates’ and teachers’ legislative council elections are notorious for the high number of invalid votes, despite the expectation that these educated voters would take care while marking their ballot papers.Election authorities, political parties and candidates repeatedly explain the dos and don’ts, yet a substantial number of ballots continue to be rejected. In the Pune division graduates’ constituency, 17,299 votes were declared invalid, while Nagpur graduates recorded 15,302 invalid votes and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 11,783.In these graduates’ constituencies, the number of invalid votes exceeded the gap between the first-preference votes secured by the leading and second-placed candidates, highlighting their potential significance in determining the outcome.The teachers’ constituencies also recorded invalid votes, with 1,673 ballots rejected in Pune and 627 in Amravati. At the beginning of counting, officials first count the ballot papers and determine how many are valid and invalid. They then calculate the winning quota—the number of valid votes a candidate must secure to be elected.These MLC elections follow a preferential voting system in which votes can be transferred according to voters’ marked preferences.Voters indicate their choices using the numerals 1, 2, 3 and so on. To help voters avoid mistakes, parties stressed that the first preference could be marked with a simple vertical stroke representing the numeral “1”, without touching the borders of the designated box. Despite these repeated instructions, large numbers of ballots were still declared invalid.Sunil Modi, Shiv Sena (UBT) candidate for Pune graduates’ seat and a co-opted corporator in Kolhapur Municipal Corporation, said invalid votes typically accounted for 8% to 10% in MLC elections in Maharashtra and other states.“We observed that voters give repetitive same preference for different candidates, there is some overwriting, some give tick marks, some write numbers such that the numeral cannot be recognized as per the given patterns. There always has been 8 to 10% such invalid votes in MLC elections not just in Maharashtra but in other states also.”According to political experts, the preferential voting system is meant for those people who are literate and can understand wholly the value of their vote.“This system was brought in exclusively for the graduates and teachers who could understand the system properly. A wise voter can give preference to all candidates as at least one of his votes of any preference can bear some value in the results. Unfortunately neither the candidates nor the voters know about the system. One mistake or a simple overwriting can make the vote invalid and the candidates will hurt eventually,” Ravindra Bhanage, professor of political science at Shivaji University, Kolhapur, said.“Since these elections are held once in six years, all stakeholders should take efforts at least from months before so that the voters are trained to cast valid votes,” said Bhanage.“The voters should realise that the winning quota of votes is determined only on the basis of valid votes. It should be imbibed in the mind of voters that one of their preferences may be useful in the end and get a clear mandate,” added the professor.More than the winners and losers, it was the messages scribbled on ballot papers that became a talking point during the two-day counting of votes for the Aurangabad graduates’ constituency, which continued until Wednesday.As ballot boxes were opened at the Chikalthana counting centre, officials found not just the prescribed preference markings, but also expressions of anger, sarcasm and despair.“Will never forgive those who change parties like clothes,” one voter wrote, expressing resentment over party-hopping. The remark appeared to target NCP candidate Satish Chavan, who had left the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction after his defeat in the 2024 assembly elections.Another ballot carried the message, “You did not even make an attempt to become our voice,” reflecting dissatisfaction with the elected representative’s performance.Frustration over unemployment also found expression, with one voter writing, “Did my degree, now I regret it!”Chavan, who has represented the constituency three times, also faced pointed remarks. “Satish, it’s done bro!” read a message found on a few ballot papers.Election authorities said names, signatures, slogans, symbols or messages that violate ballot secrecy render a vote invalid under the Conduct of Election Rules.Over 16,000 ballot papers were declared invalid during counting. “Besides those bearing messages, many were rejected because voters had failed to follow the prescribed rules for marking their preferences,” authorities said.
Article Summary: In Pune division graduates’ constituency, 17,299 votes were declared invalid. Nagpur graduates recorded 15,302 invalid votes and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 11,783. In teachers’ constituencies also recorded invalid votes, with 1,673 ballots rejected in Pune and 627 in Amravati.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.
